title: Which single number summarizing a joint bias region best predicts that a decision would flip?
question: When several bias mechanisms act together on an unanchored MAIC, does a one-at-a-time threshold report predict a decision flip as well as a minimum-norm distance or the fraction of an elicited bias distribution that preserves the decision, and does the minimum-norm answer depend on the metric?
design: DIA-13's three-mechanism bias model on an unanchored MAIC; elicited box and copula distribution with independent, positive or negative dependence; true bias drawn from the elicited law or a wider one; one-at-a-time, box, ball and preservation-fraction summaries scored against the decision flip. 24 cells, 2000 replicates each.
